newsitem.title: UK: May gas oil closes $3 higher, pushed up by buys.
newsitem.headline: May gas oil closes $3 higher, pushed up by buys.

text.p: IPE May gas oil futures settled $3 higher at $171.75 at tonne on Wednesday after a late rally on the back of buying interest, traders said.

The prompt month contract touched a high of $172 shortly before the 1630 GMT close and traded within a positive $1-$1.50 range earlier in the day. June gas oil also closed higher at $170.50 a tonne, or $2.25 over Tuesday's close.
"There has been some good quality buying in the afternoon," one broker said of gas oil.
"We did see a little bit of selling coming in in mid-afternoon but it was not ever going to hold out"
"Overall the only thing that could have led us down was heating oil but hopefully the rest of the complex is reasonably constructive and the reasonable support numbers have held out," he added.
On NYMEX, the May heating oil contract was 0.61 cents a gallon down at 58.30 cents at 1630 GMT.
Weekly American Petroleum Institute (API) data issued after the market closed on Tuesday showed U.S. distillates stocks fell 1.4 million barrels in the April 25 week.
Department of Energy figures issued on Wednesday were in line, showed a drop of 1.6 million barrels over the same period.

API also said that U.S. gasoline stocks fell a modest 408,000 barrels last week while crude stocks rose 1.87 million barrels. The corresponding Energy Department figures were a tiny rise of 100,000 barrels for gasoline and a rise of 2.8 million barrels for crude.

Earlier on Wednsday, dealers said that May gas oil would face resistance at the $170 level, but given the return to prompt backwardation some brokers said it would attempt to fill a chart gasp at $171-$172.
June Brent was maintaining its earlier lower trading levels after coming off lows briefly touched after NYMEX opened.
June Brent was trading three cents down at $18.58 a barrel by 1637 GMT.
